Subject: Payment routing for international invoices (ClearWave)

Hi Priyom,

We're ready to settle the October invoice (attached) but need a quick clarification on the best routing and how intermediary bank fees will be handled. Our AP team is in Barcelona and prefers to pay in EUR. Options on our side: SEPA to a Euro account, or send EUR via correspondent to Redwood's USD account.

Questions:
- If we send EUR via correspondent, will intermediaries likely deduct fees (so Redwood receives net)?
- Do you prefer OUR / SHA / BEN for the fee instruction?
- If intermediaries deduct, will Redwood bill us back for those fees or absorb?
- Any VAT guidance — we have an EU VAT ID but want to confirm invoicing treatment for ClearWave.

I've attached the invoice (CW_invoice_202810.pdf). Treasury also asked for sample wire fields so they can pre-populate their payment system.

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Payment routing for international invoices (ClearWave)

Hi Marta — thanks, and appreciate the heads-up. Looping Laura (billing) and Ben (payments ops) so we can give precise fields and fee guidance.

Short answers up front:
- If you send EUR to our USD account via correspondent, intermediaries commonly deduct a "correspondent/intermediary" fee; Redwood typically receives the amount net unless the sender specifies OUR.
- We prefer OUR when payers can set it, but many corporate payers default to SHA. If SHA is used, intermediary fees are usually split (payer covers sender bank, beneficiary covers receiving bank), but intermediaries en route can still deduct without explicit instruction.
- Redwood's standard approach: we do not automatically absorb random intermediary deductions. For material amounts, we re-bill the customer for the shortfall. We can be flexible if you want a fixed-fee arrangement — we can draft that into the SOW.
- VAT: since you provided an EU VAT ID, Redwood issues the invoice net of VAT for B2B intra-EU supplies where applicable. Please confirm the VAT ID exactly as it should appear on the credit note if needed.

Attached is our current wire instruction template (redwood_wire_instructions_v2.pdf). Key options to consider: SEPA EUR to our EU collection entity (no intermediaries, recommended if you can pay EUR directly), or send EUR to our US USD account with SHA/OUR tradeoffs.

Can your treasury confirm: 1) whether they can do SEPA to an EU account; or 2) if they must send to a USD account and whether they can set OUR? If they must use SHA, we will provide a fee estimate and a follow-up plan.

Next steps:
- If SEPA is possible, I'll send the EU IBAN and reference to use.
- If not, Laura will provide an estimate of expected intermediary deductions (historic ranges) and Ben will propose a reconciliation flow.

Best,
Priyom

Hi Marta / team — Laura here from Billing. Below is a pragmatic approach with historic fee ranges and a sample recovery line you can expect on your statement.

1) Historic intermediary fee ranges (EUR payer -> Redwood USD account via correspondent):
   - Single intermediary: typically $10–$25 per transfer
   - Multiple intermediaries (multi-hop): $25–$45 per transfer
   - Large banks sometimes add a fixed inline fee + percentage (rare for these volumes)

2) Preferred routing and rationale:
   - Best: SEPA EUR -> Redwood EU collection IBAN (no intermediary) — fastest and usually free on both sides.
   - Acceptable: EUR -> USD via correspondent with OUR instruction (payer to set) — ensures gross amount reaches us, but some payers cannot set OUR.
   - Fallback: EUR -> USD with SHA — we'll likely see $20–$40 deductions; we'll issue a single recovery line on your next monthly statement titled "Bank fee recovery (intermediary deductions)" with the total shortfall amount, rather than multiple micro-invoices.

3) Sample calculation (invoice €9,500):
   - If you send €9,500 via correspondent and intermediaries deduct the USD equivalent $32: Redwood will show the original invoice as paid and add one recovery line for $32 on the next statement.

4) What we need from you now:
   - Confirm you can do SEPA — if yes, we will send the EU IBAN and prefer that.
   - If SEPA is not possible, confirm whether treasury can set OUR. If neither, expect a recovery line as described.

We can also agree a small fixed monthly allowance to cover estimated recoveries if you'd like predictable billing. Ben — can you include a quick template for how we show the recovery on the invoice?

Regards,
Laura Bennett
